The World Bank estimates that about[17.5 million people work in the online gig economy across Nigeria, Kenya, and South Africa, based on its 2023 study.](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099071923114013489/pdf/P17730209c9c9502009d3b037c5b7495b42.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com) For many of these workers, the job ends on a laptop, but the payment journey is only beginning, from figuring out how to receive salary in USD in Nigeria to finding a reliable way to access and manage their earnings.


A Nigerian professional can work from Lagos for a company in New York, London, or San Francisco. The work happens remotely, but getting paid can still feel surprisingly complicated.


Should your employer send an ACH transfer? Can you receive your salary through Deel? Do you need a domiciliary account? And, perhaps most importantly, how can you receive your dollars without losing a large portion to unnecessary fees?


These questions matter more as Nigerians take on more international jobs, freelance contracts, and remote roles.


Fortunately, you have more options than a traditional bank account. With the right USD account, you can receive international payments, hold your dollars, convert them when you need naira, and spend directly in USD.


In this guide, we’ll explain how to receive salary in USD in Nigeria, the payment methods available to you, and how Cleva can help you receive and manage your international earnings.


## Can you receive salary in USD in Nigeria?


Yes, Nigerians can receive salary in USD through several payment methods.


The best option depends on how your employer processes payroll. A US company may pay you through ACH, while a global employer might use a platform such as Deel or another payroll provider.


Some companies may also pay contractors directly into a USD account.


For many remote workers, the simplest setup involves having a USD account with US banking details. Your employer or payroll platform can then send your salary directly to that account.


That is where[Cleva](http://www.getcleva.com/) comes in.


## What is the best way to receive salary in USD in Nigeria?


For most remote workers, ACH is one of the most practical ways to receive salary in USD in Nigeria when the employer supports it.


ACH stands for Automated Clearing House. It is a US payment network commonly used for direct deposits, payroll, and other bank transfers.


Instead of sending your salary through several international banking channels, your US employer can send it directly to your US account details.


Cleva supports ACH transfers into its USD accounts. ACH deposits usually arrive within one to three business days.


Cleva also supports other ways to receive USD, including wire transfers, FedNow, and supported stablecoins. FedNow payments can arrive within seconds or minutes, while ACH provides a more familiar option for recurring payments.


## 5 ways to receive salary in USD in Nigeria


### 1. Receive your salary through ACH


ACH is a strong option if your employer is based in the United States.


Your employer sends your salary using your US account and routing details. The money then arrives in your USD account without requiring your employer to send an international wire.


Cleva provides eligible users with US account details for receiving ACH payments. These details can also work with platforms that support ACH withdrawals.


This method works particularly well for remote employees with recurring monthly salaries.


### 2. Use a payroll platform such as Deel


Many international companies use payroll platforms to pay remote employees and contractors.


Deel is one example. If your employer uses Deel, you can receive your salary through the platform and select an eligible withdrawal method.


For Nigerians, using a USD account as the receiving destination can give you more control over your earnings.


Cleva can serve as your USD destination for eligible Deel payments. This allows you to receive your dollars into your Cleva account instead of immediately converting them to naira.


That flexibility matters when you want to decide when to convert your salary.


### 3. Receive your salary through a wire transfer


Some employers may prefer wire transfers, particularly for larger payments or international transactions.


Cleva supports USD wire transfers from US banks. Wire transfers can be useful when ACH is not available.


However, ACH can be more convenient for recurring salary payments when your employer supports it.


### 4. Receive your salary through another payment platform


Some remote workers receive money through platforms such as Payoneer or other payment services.


These platforms can be useful for international payments. However, fees can vary depending on how you receive and withdraw your money.


One advantage of using Cleva as your USD account is that you can receive eligible payments into one place and keep the money in USD until you decide what to do with it.


### 5. Receive USD through FedNow


FedNow offers another way to receive USD from participating US banks.


Unlike ACH, FedNow operates in real time. Cleva says eligible FedNow transfers can arrive within seconds or minutes and are available around the clock, including weekends and public holidays.


That makes it useful when speed matters.
